inputs.share_count_basis: 60.2m basic shares at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2-2026 10-Q) plus ~0.2m dilutive RSU/option equivalents = 60.4m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The ~10.6m shares to be issued to the Berghmans family on Lhoist North America closing are NOT in this count because the Lhoist cash flows are not in the model either (standalone basis; see notes).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $46m plus $31m cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement (financing). MLM publishes no combined equity-award figure in its adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $450m (FY2024 $450m, H1-2026 $200m). MLM is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention; share count fell 62.5m (FY2022) to 60.2m (Q2-2026).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the last completed fiscal year (FY2025, Dec-25). Y1 = FY2026, the guidance year, discounted a full period although three quarters have elapsed at the valuation date -- a conservative timing bias of roughly 5% on value. Net debt is the 30-Jun-2026 balance; H1-2026 owner FCF was approximately -$43m (reported FCF $25m less $68m SBC and equity taxes, depressed by ~$300m cash tax on the Quikrete exchange gain and seasonal working capital), so counting the full FY2026 flow as Y1 against the June balance sheet double-counts a negligible amount.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.95 = ~9.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (3.9% after tax) on ~19% debt weight (net debt $6.7bn against $28.9bn market cap) = ~8.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality, energy-cost and Lhoist integration risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842): operating lease cost (quarry land/mineral leases, equipment) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, and `total_debt` is bonds, notes and commercial paper only -- operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Treatment (B), applied once. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.interest_income_note: Cash of $112m against $6.8bn of debt -- net cash is not material, so no interest-income strip and no cash pile in the bridge.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: The DB `ebitda` column is operating income + D&A (FY2025 $2,074m, 33.7% of revenue). Management's adjusted EBITDA adds back acquisition/divestiture and deal costs (~$60m in Q2-2026 alone, Lhoist and New Frontier). FY2026 guidance of $2.36-2.50bn is adjusted; the Y1 margin paths bracket 32.5-33.6% to give partial credit for add-backs while treating a share of the recurring deal costs as real.
inputs.lhoist_note: The ~$13.5bn Lhoist North America combination ($7bn cash + ~$6.5bn stock, ~10.6m shares, ~15% of the post-close count) was announced June 2026 and is pending regulatory approval, expected to close H2-2026. It is NOT modelled: Lhoist NA's standalone financials are not in the filings, and at the implied ~13-15x EBITDA against MLM's own ~14.6x EV/EBITDA the deal with $85m of targeted run-rate synergies is approximately value-neutral per share at the announcement price. This is a STANDALONE valuation of Martin Marietta as it exists at 30-Jun-2026 (post-Quikrete exchange, post-New Frontier). The bear case carries the acquirer risks (overpayment, integration drag, leverage into a construction downturn) through its margin and growth paths; the bull case does not credit the synergies. Rebuild on a pro-forma basis once the deal closes and the first combined 10-Q discloses Lhoist's contribution.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year explicit horizon (margins and capex intensity are still normalising from the FY2024-25 plant-capex peak and the cement exit). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, cyclical industrial) with the owner-fcf-adaptations file read: single lease treatment (B), no NCI, no excluded income, SBC present (not SBC-zero), risk charged once in the flows. Fresh build -- no prior DCF or memory entry. Revenue base is FY2025 total revenue $6,150m (XBRL series; the Analysis JSON's '$5.7bn continuing' figure is a press-release subset and is not used -- the $7.2-7.4bn FY2026 guide and the +19% H1-2026 print are only consistent with the $6,150m base). Working capital is charged on the change in revenue at -8%: receivables + inventories exceed payables for an aggregates producer, so growth consumes cash (FY2025 OCF $1,785m against NI + D&A + SBC $1,820m on +$488m revenue).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.2% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 5.4%: equity was inflated by divestiture gains (FY2024 South Texas cement sale to CRH, Q1-2026 Quikrete exchange gain of ~$1.3bn in net income), not by operating compounding. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor; the revenue CAGR (5.4%, through the cement/concrete exits and bolt-on aggregates acquisitions) is the long-run organic reference, and FY2026 is set by guidance.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes (FY2020 $646m, FY2022 $437m, FY2025 $901m). Owner-FCF CAGRs run ~1pp below reported (27.3% vs 24.3% 3yr is a base-year artefact: FY2022 was a capex-heavy, working-capital-heavy trough). SBC is ~1.2% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow. 3-year revenue CAGR is ~0% because FY2022 included the since-divested cement and ready-mix businesses; it is not an organic signal. EPS CAGRs (FY2022 $13.91 to FY2025 $18.81) are clean of the gain years at both endpoints.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 18.5% lands FY2026 revenue at $7.29bn, the midpoint of the raised $7.2-7.4bn guide (H1-2026 +19.4%; Quikrete aggregates from Feb-26 and New Frontier from May-26). Y2 7% = ~1.5pp of New Frontier annualisation plus mid-single-digit pricing and low-single-digit volume; thereafter decays from 6% to 3% as IIJA peak-spend (2026-27) rolls off and pricing normalises toward the 5.4% 10-year revenue CAGR, then below it.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 33.7% (op income + D&A). FY2026 guide midpoint ($2.43bn adjusted on $7.3bn) is 33.3%; 33.0% gives partial credit for deal-cost add-backs and reflects the energy-cost headwind management flagged for H2-2026. +50bp/yr to 35% by Y5 is the historical aggregates pattern of price outrunning unit cost (aggregates gross margin +140-170bp/yr in FY2024-25) plus the mix shift away from asphalt/paving and cement.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2026 capex guided ~$575m (8% of revenue, down 29% from FY2025's $807m / 13.1% as plant projects complete). Capex steps back to 9.5% long run against 10.0% D&A: FY2019-22 capex ran 7.6-8.3% of revenue when D&A was 8-8.5%, and D&A is now inflated by depletion on acquired reserves (FY2025 10.4%, H1-2026 11.2%), so capex modestly below D&A is the historical relationship, not a flattering one.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 22% flat: GAAP effective rate ~20-22% (21% federal + state, net of percentage depletion); FY2025 cash taxes $192m were timing-depressed and H1-2026 $296m carries the Quikrete gain, so neither year is a base.

scenario_narratives.base: Aggregates-led compounding continues as it has for a decade: mid-single-digit pricing on a locally permitted, freight-protected reserve base, low-single-digit volumes, and ~50bp a year of margin expansion as price outruns unit cost. FY2026 lands on the raised $7.2-7.4bn guide with the EBITDA guide held (energy costs absorb the revenue beat). IIJA peak disbursement in 2026-27 and Sun Belt data-centre/power construction offset soft residential and private nonresidential work; growth decays toward 3% by the end of the decade as the federal programme rolls off. Capex normalises to ~9.5% of revenue after the FY2024-25 plant build-out. Lhoist North America is treated as value-neutral and excluded.
scenario_narratives.bull: The infrastructure and data-centre cycle extends: IIJA is reauthorised at or above current levels in 2027, residential recovers on lower rates, and MLM's Sun Belt footprint takes an outsized share of the power-grid and reshoring build. Pricing stays mid-to-high single digits with volumes positive every year, so margins climb to 37% -- the pure-play aggregates level the SOAR portfolio strategy has been targeting -- and capex settles at 9% of revenue. Lhoist closes and the $85m synergy target is met, but no credit is taken for it here.
scenario_narratives.bear: Energy costs stay elevated and unhedged, IIJA disbursements fade after 2027 without a comparable successor, and a rate-driven construction recession takes private nonresidential and residential volumes down together in 2028 (revenue flat, margin trough at 30%). Into that downturn MLM is carrying ~$7bn of Lhoist acquisition debt and a 15% larger share count, so bolt-on M&A and buybacks stop while synergies lag; pricing holds but cannot outrun cost. Margins recover only to 32% and growth settles at 3%, with a 15x terminal cap reflecting a leveraged cyclical rather than a compounder.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the business is entering a transformational, debt-funded acquisition (largest in its history, ~45% of the current market cap) at the same time management is flagging an unhedged energy-cost margin squeeze, and the stock has made repeated 52-week lows on guidance disappointments -- the bear case is a plausible combination of leverage and a construction downturn, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right: IIJA reauthorisation beyond 2027, a residential recovery, and the data-centre build continuing at pace. Base 50%: the aggregates pricing franchise is the most reliable element and a decade of mid-single-digit price growth through cycles supports it being the central case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Martin Marietta is valued as a standalone owner of a locally monopolistic, permit-protected aggregates reserve base: the model capitalises the cash the quarries throw off after real reinvestment, SBC and cash tax, at a USD WACC of 8%, with cyclicality and the Lhoist leverage/integration risk carried in the scenario paths and weights rather than in the discount rate. The FY2024-25 capex peak and the cement exit mean trailing FCF understates the run-rate, so the forward build starts from guided FY2026 capex of ~$575m and lets capex normalise to 9.5% of revenue rather than carrying the 13% trailing intensity forward. The valuation is deliberately pre-Lhoist: the deal is roughly value-neutral per share at the announced terms, and modelling it from press-release figures would add assumption risk without adding information.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lhoist North America: ~$7bn of new debt and ~10.6m new shares (~15% dilution) on a deal whose standalone economics are not in the filings; overpayment or synergy shortfall is not in the base case, and regulatory divestitures could change the terms
Energy and diesel cost inflation compressing unit margins faster than mid-single-digit pricing can recover (the explicit reason FY2026 EBITDA guidance was held while revenue guidance rose)
IIJA reimbursements peak in 2026-27 with no successor programme yet legislated; the growth path decays but does not go negative, which assumes an orderly roll-off
Construction-cycle sensitivity of volumes (residential, private nonresidential) and Texas/Southeast weather concentration
Terminal value is 18x FCF-capped and roughly two-thirds of enterprise value; each 1pp of WACC moves the base value by roughly 15%
Year-1 is discounted a full period although three quarters of FY2026 have elapsed -- a ~5% conservative timing bias
